note: Legs v1 are robotai's own design (cad/legs_v1.py, Blender), built for dynamic moves: 7 joints per leg, big drives at hip and knee, ankle drives in the calf with push rods. 'match' is a regex on part / joint names in the GLB.

stages.title: Learn to walk in simulation
stages.text: Train a walking policy for this exact robot in MuJoCo, starting from the ToddlerBot and Open Duck code. No hardware needed yet.

stages.title: Build the real walker
stages.text: If the torso build is on schedule and at least C$400 is left: a small 0.62 m servo walker, about C$390, to prove the walking code on real hardware.

stages.title: Dynamic full-size legs
stages.text: The legs shown: brushless quasi-direct-drive joints strong enough to run, jump and flip with the ~9 kg InMoov upper body, roughly C$200-400 per joint. That's the next budget.

parts.name: Hips
parts.actuator: 3 brushless drives per hip; the pitch drive is the biggest, it powers jumps and kicks

parts.name: Thigh + knee
parts.actuator: Brushless knee drive with a printed low-backlash gearbox; kneecap shell protects it

parts.name: Calf + ankle drives
parts.actuator: Two drives sit high in the calf and push the foot through rods, so the lower leg stays light for fast swings
parts.made: Printed calf shell, carbon push rods

parts.name: Foot + toe
parts.actuator: Toe joint for push-off when running and jumping

parts.name: Pelvis
parts.actuator: Bolts under the InMoov torso; IMU for balance lives here
